verdict_summary: The audit is deep on code mechanics and market comps but has a blind hemisphere: it never analyzes data privacy/confidentiality, local-compute COGS, content licensing of fetched sources, i18n/accessibility, or the legal/contract layer — and several of its own recommended business wedges (pharma, defense/intel, 'reproducible evidence synthesis') are directly contradicted by code findings the audit itself confirmed but never cross-referenced. At least two analyst contradictions (model_usage.jsonl existence; a refuted path-traversal finding still listed as a production gap) made it into the final digest unreconciled, and the single number the business case turns on — the cost to build the L5 verification moat — is estimated nowhere.

points.title: Data privacy / GDPR / confidentiality: entirely missing dimension
points.argument: Across 10 analysts there is one passing clause ('free-tier ToS/data-training exposure unaddressed'). Nobody analyzed: runs/{run_id}/ retains the full uploaded document, all LLM outputs, and the S1 interview-derived UserProfile (reader profiling = personal data under GDPR Art. 4) indefinitely with no deletion endpoint, no encryption at rest, no retention policy; user documents fan out to 5+ subprocessors (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google API, Groq, Mistral, plus the geminicli free OAuth tier whose consumer terms grant Google training rights); no DPA/subprocessor inventory exists; prod-patterns noted Anthropic batch mode is not ZDR-eligible but never connected that to the proposed pharma wedge. This matters because the audit's own #1 GTM recommendation — pharma medical affairs handling confidential pre-publication evidence — is a confidentiality-first buyer; without a data-handling story the recommended business case is unsellable regardless of code quality.

points.title: Defense/intel wedge contradicts the architecture: pipeline cannot run air-gapped
points.argument: The market analyst recommends defense/intel analyst onboarding (Primer's segment) as wedge #3. No analyst noted the pipeline is structurally cloud-bound: every stage depends on live external APIs (Wikipedia, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, arXiv, PyPI in sources.py/bibliography.py), frontier LLM APIs, an npx-spawned Google OAuth CLI, and a first-run HuggingFace download of BGE-M3 weights (s2_extract.py imports SentenceTransformer('BAAI/bge-m3')). Defense/intel buyers require on-prem/air-gapped or IL4+ deployment. This wedge should either be struck from the GTM list or costed as a separate offline product (local models + offline corpus mirrors) — the audit does neither.

points.title: 'Reproducible, auditable evidence synthesis' positioning is refuted by confirmed routing findings — never cross-referenced
points.argument: The business analyst proposes repositioning as 'reproducible, auditable evidence synthesis' for pharma. The llm-routing analyst confirmed: quota-driven nondeterministic model substitution mid-run, no temperature/max_tokens control anywhere, and cost/model-mix logging (model_usage.jsonl) that does not exist in code. A run's model mix cannot be reproduced or even described post-hoc. GxP/audit-trail buyers require exactly the per-call provenance record the README fakes. The audit contains both halves of this contradiction and never connects them; the fix (persist actual model, params, prompt hash per call) is cheap and should be a named prerequisite of the pharma pivot.

points.title: Local compute / infra COGS unanalyzed; all unit economics are token-only
points.argument: uv.lock (/Users/cyan/ccr/know-expand/uv.lock) pins torch, torchvision, transformers, accelerate, docling-ibm-models, sentence-transformers — a multi-GB install plus ~2.3GB BGE-M3 weights and Docling layout models downloaded at first run. No analyst measured S0 (Docling CPU parse) or S2 (KeyBERT+BGE-M3 embedding) wall-clock, RAM footprint per concurrent run (plausibly 8-12GB), container image size, or GPU-vs-CPU server pricing. The market analysis prices runs at $100-500 against token cost alone, and even the README's $50-150/deep-run token estimate (README.md:43) was never validated against actual prompt sizes. The hosted-product margin math — the core of the business case — has no compute, storage, bandwidth, or HITL-operator-time line items.

points.title: xelatex/pandoc: operational burden and an unflagged LaTeX-injection vector
points.argument: s10_assemble.py:574-580 invokes pandoc with --pdf-engine=xelatex and no --sandbox flag, so raw LaTeX in LLM-generated (or source-document-derived) markdown passes through to xelatex, where default TeX Live openin_any settings allow \input-style reads of server files into the shipped PDF — a data-exfiltration vector for a hosted product compiling untrusted content; no analyst examined it. Separately unanalyzed: TeX Live adds 2-5GB to any image, font/Unicode coverage failures on arbitrary LLM math output are a recurring support class (the audit found the math-fixer incoherence but not the ops burden), pandoc is GPL-2+ (fine as subprocess, but image redistribution carries a source-offer obligation), and no alternative (Typst, HTML+print CSS) was evaluated.

points.title: Content licensing of fetched third-party sources: the real license exposure, not analyzed
points.argument: quality-risk covered the source-paper derivative-work question thoroughly but never the inbound content: Wikipedia extracts (sources.py:116-181, en.wikipedia hardcoded) are CC BY-SA — share-alike text injected into S5 persona prompts and paraphrased into a commercial PDF raises attribution/SA obligations with no attribution mechanism in the output; Semantic Scholar abstracts (stored in audit caches and used by S8) are publisher-licensed with redistribution restrictions under S2's ODC-BY/dataset terms; OpenAlex is CC0 (fine). Also concrete: sources.py:51 sends OpenAlex a fake polite-pool identity 'mailto:research@example.com' — a ToS-etiquette violation that risks rate-deprioritization and is indefensible in a commercial product.

points.title: Dependency code-license review was never done — it is actually clean, and saying so closes a risk cheaply
points.argument: pyproject.toml deps check out for commercial use: docling MIT (IBM), keybert MIT, sentence-transformers Apache-2.0, BGE-M3 model weights MIT, spaCy + en_core_web_sm MIT, litellm MIT, instructor MIT, langgraph MIT, pypdf BSD; the project itself ships MIT (LICENSE, copyright Anas Ahmed 2026). The only copyleft touchpoints are pandoc (GPL-2+) and TeX Live components, both invoked as subprocesses — compliance burden is a source-offer if redistributed in an image. The audit left this as an open unknown; it should be recorded as resolved so the licensing risk register correctly points at content (previous point) and the geminicli consumer ToS, not code.

points.title: English-only pipeline ceiling: i18n never assessed against the market sizing
points.argument: Hardcoded: en.wikipedia.org endpoints (sources.py:120,139), KeyBERT stop_words='english' (s2_extract.py:87), spaCy en_core_web_sm (a CLAUDE.md constraint), English-language prompts throughout. Non-English source papers and non-English deliverables are unsupported. The market analysis sizes against global pharma, EU consulting, and a $400B corporate-training market without noting the product addresses only the English slice, and no analyst listed i18n cost in the production-readiness gap lists.

points.title: Accessibility unexamined: untagged PDFs and an inaccessible web UI
points.argument: xelatex output is not tagged PDF (no PDF/UA), and the observe.py dashboard has no accessibility consideration at all. The European Accessibility Act has applied to consumer-facing digital services since June 2025; B2B-only positioning reduces but does not eliminate exposure (enterprise procurement increasingly requires VPAT/WCAG statements, and US federal/defense buyers require Section 508). Zero analysts mentioned accessibility; it belongs in the production-gap list with a calibrated (medium, wedge-dependent) weight.

points.title: Direct analyst contradiction: model_usage.jsonl 'fiction' vs 'logged but never acted on'
points.argument: llm-routing (confirmed) states cost tracking 'does not exist anywhere in the code' — verified correct: grep shows model_usage.jsonl appears only in README.md (lines 43, 723, 830, 969), never in know_expand/. But stages-late's production_gaps asserts 'model_usage.jsonl is logged but never acted on', a false claim that survived into the final digest. Any remediation plan that trusts the stages-late line will assume a cost-data foundation that does not exist. The digest needs a reconciliation pass where production_gaps entries inherit the verification verdicts.

points.title: Refuted finding still presented as a production gap: /api/section path traversal
points.argument: The webui verification table records 'Path traversal in /api/section reads arbitrary .md files' as refuted, yet the same subsystem's production_gaps list restates '/api/section traverses to arbitrary .md files' as fact. Beyond this instance, the gap lists across all subsystems freely mix confirmed, partially_confirmed, and never-verified claims with identical confidence — e.g., the '~37% chunk truncation' (partially_confirmed) and '4-10x persona cost' (partially_confirmed, unmeasured) are cited as flat facts in summaries. A severity-weighted plan built on this digest will mis-rank work.

points.title: Unresolved strategy contradictions: the audit hands the owner three incompatible roadmaps
points.argument: (a) Human-in-the-loop: market says S1/S3 are differentiators to keep as premium; stages-early rates the mandatory interview a critical blocker for multi-user operation; business says reposition as expert-review checkpoints. (b) Pedagogy: market declares the pedagogically-structured 200-page book the entire white space; business says 'no identified enterprise buyer pays for pedagogical beauty — expect to cut those layers.' (c) Pricing: market endorses $100-500 per-artifact (Kosmos anchor); business warns any per-report price anchored near $200 loses. (d) Platform: prod-patterns says keep LangGraph and add a SqliteSaver checkpointer; orchestration says LangGraph is a decorative facade and multi-user requires admitting a rewrite boundary; prod-patterns says shrink observe.py, webui says ground-up redesign. The audit contains no adjudication layer; without one, 'production ready' has no agreed definition of done.

points.title: The claimed moat is the weakest verified subsystem, and the cost to build it is estimated nowhere
points.argument: All four research topics converge on 'verification is the product' (L5 claim-level entailment, per-run verification reports, >95% support rate). All code analysts converge on verification being L1 theater with confirmed broken wiring (S7 cites from an empty bibliography pool; S6 injects phantom citation keys; S10 strips the markers). The single number the entire business case depends on — engineering effort/$/time to go from L1 to a shippable L5 'verified' SKU, including the DOI-resolution pass, entailment checks against stored abstracts, and the in-document flagging UX — appears in no analysis. Quality-risk sketches the technical path but never sizes it; the business analysis assumes it exists when ranking wedges.

points.title: Model lifecycle risk: the free tier the entire cost structure leans on runs a preview model via unpinned npx
points.argument: The default cheap-first economics depend on geminicli spawning npx @google/gemini-cli with gemini-3.1-pro-preview (per CLAUDE.md and confirmed silent-aliasing finding). Preview models are withdrawn without notice, the CLI package is unpinned, and Google has repeatedly tightened free OAuth quotas. No analyst modeled the scenario where the free path disappears: every role's cost floor jumps to paid API rates, invalidating both the $5-20 standard-run estimate and the cheap-first routing design. A production plan needs pinned versions, a deprecation watch, and a costed 'no-free-tier' fallback budget.

points.title: Liability/contract layer and certification costs named but never sized
points.argument: quality-risk covers FTC deceptive-claims and copyright well, but the audit omits: E&O/professional liability insurance for selling 'verified' research deliverables; the gap between the MIT 'AS IS' disclaimer and the warranties/indemnities pharma and consulting buyers demand in MSAs; and the actual cost/timeline of the certifications the business analysis itself names as cost-of-entry (SOC 2 Type II is roughly $30-80k plus 6-12 months; GxP/CSV validation more). Also absent at the ops layer: backup/DR for runs/ (the only copy of a paid deliverable), bus-factor-1 maintainership, and a support model for LaTeX build failures on customer documents. These are line items the wedge ranking should have priced.
